p.espaces.rg_d: Customs, product standards, starting a business, investment platforms: official sources of each country.
p.espaces.rg_sub: Rules change often: ONE WORLD does not copy them, it opens up the official sources to update, then you read them in your language.
p.espaces.rg_g1: World Trade Helpdesk (ITC, UNCTAD, WTO): duties, taxes, rules and procedures on one page for your product and country
p.espaces.rg_g2: Market Access Map (MAM): customs duties and rules of origin
p.espaces.rg_g3: ePing (WTO): standards, labelling and health rules that this country sets for products
p.espaces.rg_e1: Market access: trade with and from the EU, step by step
p.espaces.rg_e2: TARIC: customs code and duties when you enter the EU
p.espaces.rg_b1: Business Ready (World Bank): starting a business, taxes, international trade, country by country
p.espaces.rg_i1: I-SCAN (IOSCO): check a platform is not covered by a regulator before you entrust money to it
p.espaces.rg_note: Opens a site in your own language: use the translation of your browser, or « Understand a document » for documents.For an important decision, ask a professional in that country.
p.espaces.cu_d: Duties, documents, Incoterms, free official tools, shippers and carriers.
p.espaces.cu_sub: 24/24 ONE WORLD does not file customs declarations: a licensed customs broker (freight forwarder) can do it for you.
p.espaces.cu_t1: Market Access Map (ITC, UN-WTO): duties and rules for almost every country
p.espaces.cu_t2: Access2Markets (EU): duties, taxes, rules of origin, step by step
p.espaces.cu_t3: TARIC: customs code (HS code) and duties when entering the EU
p.espaces.cu_d3: Transport document: bills of lading (sea), air waybill (air), CMR (road)
p.espaces.cu_d4: Certificate of origin (to receive reduced duties)
p.espaces.cu_d5: EORI number (EU importing or exporting businesses)
p.espaces.cu_d6: Depending on the product: health or phytosanitary certificate, licence, CE standards
p.espaces.cu_i1: EXW: everything is handled by buyer from seller's factory.
p.espaces.cu_i2: FCA: the seller delivers the export cleared goods to the buyer’s carrier.
p.espaces.cu_i3: FOB: the seller loads on the ship; afterwards, risks and costs are the buyer’s.
p.espaces.cu_i4: CIF: the seller pays freight and insurance to the port of arrival.
p.espaces.cu_i5: DAP: the seller delivers to a destination, the buyer pays import duties.
p.espaces.cu_i6: DDP: the seller pays everything, including import duties.
p.espaces.cu_ban: Prohibition or control everywhere: weapons, drugs, counterfeits, protected species (CITES), some medicines. Such lists are rejected and can be reported (en).
p.espaces.cu_src: Sources: ICC (Incoterms 2020), ITC, European Commission, douane.gouv.fr Always check the exact rules for your product.

p.espaces.mt_d: Western Union, MoneyGram, Wise, Remitly... compare the fees for your country before you send.
p.espaces.mt_sub: 24/24 ONE WORLD does not put money itself and does not earn anything from these links: you compare here, then you will be sent to the service of your choice.
p.espaces.mt_wb: Remittance Prices Worldwide (World Bank): the real cost of sending money, by country, by service
p.espaces.mt_p_wu: Money collection in many countries, bank transfer, mobile wallet
p.espaces.mt_p_mg: Cash collection, bank transfer, mobile wallet
p.espaces.mt_p_wise: Bank transfer at market exchange rate, fees shown before you send
p.espaces.mt_p_rem: Bank transfer, mobile wallet, cash pick up
p.espaces.mt_p_wr: Mobile wallet, bank transfer, cash pick up
p.espaces.mt_p_tt: Send to mobile wallet or bank account
p.espaces.mt_k1: See the total received: fees + exchange rate A worse than market rate is a hidden cost.
p.espaces.mt_k2: Choose how the person receives it: cash, bank account or mobile wallet (M-Pesa, Orange Money, MTN...).
p.espaces.mt_k3: An identity document is often required, for sending and collecting it.
p.espaces.mt_k4: Never send money to someone you only met online, or to "unlock" a prize, parcel, loan or visa: it is almost always a scam.
p.espaces.mt_note: Services and price changes: always check their website when you ship.
p.espaces.ds_d: Selling without stock: find a supplier, work out the real price, stay within the law.
p.espaces.ds_sub: Dropshipping means selling a product that the supplier sends directly to your customer. Easy to start, but you are responsible for the sale.
p.espaces.ds_s1: Choose a product that is approved in your customer’s country: no counterfeit, no unauthorised regulated product.
p.espaces.ds_s2: Find a supplier ("Wholesale/supplier" listings here or wholesale platforms) and order a sample before you sell.
p.espaces.ds_s3: Work out the real price: product, shipping, customs duties, VAT of the customer's country, payment fees and returns.
p.espaces.ds_s4: Tell customers the actual delivery time.
p.espaces.ds_s5: Register your activity: business status, VAT and taxes according to your country (see trade rules).
p.espaces.ds_s6: Respecting consumers' rights: clear prices including taxes, right of return, warranty, data protection.
p.espaces.ds_w1: A supplier who wants full payment by unsecured bank transfer or in cryptocurrency.
p.espaces.ds_w2: Paid courses that promise to make you rich quickly.
p.espaces.ds_w3: Stolen photos and fake reviews: prohibition and punishment.
p.espaces.ds_w4: In the European Union, a non-EU action pays VAT from the first euro.
